articles.title: World Bank's $100 billion crisis cushion
articles.summary: Bangkok: The World Bank is in discussions with 30 to 40 countries about potential crisis aid to help them manage energy shocks and price increases triggered by the war in the Middle East, its president, Ajay Banga, told Reuters in an interview.Banga said the global economy had proven fairly resilient, in part due to big AI investments and adjustments in supply and demand for oil, which meant that few countries had sought the initial $25 billion in crisis funds that the World Bank had made available when the war began in late February.Also Read: World Bank raises India FY27 growth forecast to 7.1%, flags oil, El Niño risksHowever, a sharp spike in diesel and fertilizer prices and other factors, including the looming super El Nino weather effect, were adding to challenges facing developing countries, Banga said in an interview ahead of this week's annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank."There is pressure, and so I think maybe over the coming months, more countries will come for some slice of that first $50 to $60 billion," Banga said, referring to the initial $25 billion plus another $35 billion that countries could tap by diverting resources from already approved World Bank projects."We'll see, but we're ready. We're engaged. We're having conversations with a number of them, you know, 30 to 40 countries are in dialogue with us," he said.Many developing countries have been hit hard by the spike in energy prices and high interest rates that have increased borrowing costs at a time when their fiscal coffers are still depleted by measures taken during the COVID-19 pandemic and the spike in inflation following Russia's invasion of Ukraine.World Bank estimates show that developing countries owe external creditors about $400 billion in 2026, with interest payments alone comprising one-third of the total.Banga said more countries had shown interest in retooling existing projects than in tapping the immediate crisis window to address their liquidity needs. If the situation worsened, the Bank could make available as much as $100 billion in funds, he said, exceeding the $70 billion disbursed during the pandemic.The World Bank last month announced that it attracted a record $112 billion in private capital in the year ended June versus $69 billion a year earlier, and more than triple the 2022 total before Banga, a former Mastercard CEO, became president.Also Read: World Bank mobilises $112 billion in private capital for developing nationsThat was on top of the $123 billion invested from the bank's own resources for that year, for a combined $235 billion, Banga said, underscoring the importance of tapping all available resources, especially at a time when Western countries have sharply cut official bilateral development aid."There is no one answer that fits when the world has these kinds of issues. What you need to do is figure out how to cut your coat to suit your cloth," Banga said.Banga said he expected further gains in private capital flows in coming years, aided by expanded political risk guarantees from the bank's Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency, growth in local currency financing, and continued work on regulatory reforms that made it easier for foreign investors.The private capital jump was biggest in projects in upper-middle-income countries like Argentina or India, which accounted for $50 billion of the private capital, and lower-middle-income countries including Bangladesh and Angola, which accounted for $37 billion. But more work was needed to boost the roughly $3 billion in private capital flowing to low-income countries."In the smaller countries, it hasn't multiplied enough, and there are challenges," he said, noting the bank would announce some new initiatives this week aimed at ensuring micro-, small- and medium-sized businesses also had access to private capital.Banga said private capital growth was also regionally spread, with the largest increase seen in Latin America and the Caribbean, which accounted for $36.3 billion of last year's total, followed by Europe and Central Asia with $21.3 billion, South Asia with $19.2 billion and Africa with $22 billion.The top 10 recipient countries were Brazil, India, Turkey, Romania, Nigeria, Argentina, South Africa, Bangladesh, Mexico and Chile, the Bank said.Banga said the World Bank and IMF were working together to address the high debt levels plaguing many developing countries through a series of initiatives, including efforts to boost countries' domestic revenue collections.The Bank had already set up some debt-for-development swaps for Angola and Ivory Coast, and a portfolio-based guarantee for Argentina, and was working on over a dozen more projects."We've got 14 or 15 in the pipeline, helping them rotate out higher-priced old debt for newer-priced debt with our guarantees," with the difference then targeted at education, healthcare, water, or nature programs, he said.

articles.summary: Kathmandu: A debris-laden flash flood in a river has swept away more than 35 houses and bridges in Nepal's Gorkha district on Sunday, authorities said, urging people living along the stream to move to higher ground.The flood in the Budhi Gandaki River swept away houses in Salleri, Paiyuka and the riverbed at Jagat, as well as a suspension bridge connecting the ward, Ram Kumar Gurung, ward chair of Chumnubri Rural Municipality-3, was quoted as saying by the Kathmandu Post.Also Read: Nepal floods: 1,453 dead, nearly 5,300 still missing a month after disasterDharmendra Kumar Mishra, Gorkha's chief district officer, said preliminary reports indicated that a landslide had occurred above Siuribas. No casualties have been reported so far, he said.The cause of the sudden surge remained unclear. Residents suspect that the Syar stream, a tributary of the Budhi Gandaki between Lokpa and Chumling in Chumnubri-6, may have been blocked, triggering the flood.The flash flood in the river swept away more than 35 houses in several locations in northern Gorkha, officials said.Also Read: Nepal wraps up Rasuwa flood search; shifts focus to rehabilitation, reconstructionChumnubri Rural Municipality Deputy Chair Laxmi Gurung said the flood that hit the Budhi Gandaki this morning is reminiscent of the Bhotekoshi flood in Rasuwa, Online Khabar news portal reported."The Budhigandaki flood is reminiscent of the Bhotekoshi flood," she said. "It has washed away dozens of houses. It is not possible to say the exact extent of the damage right now."The devastating flooding struck the Bhote Koshi River in Rasuwa district on August 26. The floods in the Rasuwa and Trishuli river areas claimed 1,455 lives, while 5,285 people remained missing, according to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA).Home Minister Sudan Gurung said the flood had also swept away the bridge linking Nyakchet and Philim bazaar in Chumnubri-3. With the river continuing to rise, helicopters had been deployed for rescue operations, relief distribution and evacuations, he said.Nepal Police, the Armed Police Force and local authorities were mobilised to carry out rescue and relief operations."The flood came early in the morning, and we could not even take out our belongings," Ram Kumar said."Everyone fled as soon as we heard the flood was coming." The full extent of the damage was not yet known, he said.Residents in riverside settlements, including Chumling and Lokpa, fled their homes after hearing loud roaring sounds from the streams from around 4am. Tourists staying at local hotels also fled, residents said.Sherap Gurung, a resident of Lokpa, said the sound suggested that the water flow had repeatedly stopped and resumed."Because it was dark, we could not tell whether the stream had been blocked or a landslide had occurred. It had not rained either," he said.Authorities were using loudspeakers to warn people living along the river and urge them to move to safer locations.

articles.title: India condemns attack on Saudi airport that killed 12, injured over 300
articles.summary:
India on Sunday strongly condemned a major attack on Saudi Arabia's international airport in Riyadh that killed 12 people and injured over 300.
New Delhi said the repeated attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure in the Gulf nation are "completely unacceptable and must cease immediately."
"We strongly condemn the repeated attacks on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport over the past few days, including the dastardly attack on October 10, which have led to loss of lives, injuries and damage to property," the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said in a statement.
"We express our condolences to the families of the deceased and wish speedy recovery to the injured persons," it said.
Saudi Arabia has blamed Houthi militants for the attack.
"We stand in solidarity with the people and the government of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in defence of their sovereignty, and hope that peace and normalcy returns to the region at the earliest," the MEA said.

He wants to make problems for our farmers, our ranchers, with diesel fuel," Trump said, before departing for Tennessee where he was set to rally Republican voters.An Associated Press-NORC Centre for Public Affairs Research poll conducted last month and published Oct 1 found that Americans disapprove of Trump's handling of Iran, and blame him for higher prices.Trump also suggested that if he had been US president in 2022, "that war would have never started. There was no reason that that war with Ukraine and Russia started. It started due to incompetence."Zelenskyy has "lost 30% of your country and you've had over a million people go between the two of them, over 2 million people killed. That's a war that should have never started. And I think it's time for Ukraine to get a new president," Trump said.Independent estimates are that about 20 per cent of Ukraine's territory is under Russian control.British defence officials recently estimated that about half a million Russian soldiers have been killed in the war; there are no reliable recent estimates about how many Ukrainians have died.Trump's extraordinary intervention came after Russian strikes killed at least 20 people in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, Ukrainian officials said Saturday.Three children were among those killed when Russian aerial bombs hit residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine's State Emergency Service said Saturday. At least 18 people were wounded.Russia and Ukraine are locked in a long-range aerial war while their armies remain largely deadlocked on the front line, more than 4 1/2 years since Moscow's full-scale invasion.Ukraine is struggling to counter escalating Russian bombardments that have killed more than 60 people over the past four days."Today, Russia expressed its thanks for the lifting of sanctions on diesel exports by dropping five glide bombs on residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia," Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy wrote Saturday on X.He said the attacks show Moscow understands "any easing of pressure to mean they can keep fighting, to mean they can keep dropping bombs on cities.""Russia's choice is war," Zelenskyy said in a later Telegram post, after drone attacks on energy facilities and a ballistic missile attack on Kyiv.He said every additional billion dollars Russia earns from exports would help pay for weapons components, drone upgrades, missile production and the recruitment of mercenaries, and that Moscow would only be ready to stop when its ability to fight diminished.Moscow received from diesel deal "signals that it is apparently permissible to continue attacking. And this needs to be corrected," he said, urging the US, Europe and other partners to limit Russia's capacity to wage war.Zelenskyy said Ukraine was coordinating steps to counter the extra revenue Russia will receive, and that he had spoken to French President Emmanuel Macron about shoring up air defences, warning of an increased risk of further missile strikes in the coming days.He also said he had discussed the developments with Finnish President Alexander Stubb, and that Ukraine would receive ammunition in the coming days for the F-16s it uses to intercept Shahed drones.Trump had been set to discuss a suspected case of plague in Russia with President Vladimir Putin in a phone call.Instead, the American leader announced Friday that Russia will immediately supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel, followed by an additional 500,000 tons in November and 1 million tons "immediately thereafter".Russia will deliver an additional 3 million tons "within a short period of time" after that, he wrote.In Kyiv, people gathered at a memorial to fallen soldiers on Independence Square greeted the deal with a mix of anger and resignation."Trump has once again shown his true face," said Oleksandr Petrenko, 26. Police have detained more than 200 people, while restrictions on Metro services, internet access and road traffic have affected movement across parts of the national capital.CJP founders detained at Delhi airportDelhi Police personnel entered an aircraft carrying CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke after it landed at IGI Airport on Saturday, ahead of the planned demonstration at Jantar Mantar.In a video of the incident, Dipke is heard telling police personnel, “I have come here to be arrested; arrest me.”The police personnel respond, “No, this is not an arrest. Please cooperate.”— ANI (@ANI) Dipke had travelled to Delhi to join the CJP's planned protest. The party said its founders Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das were detained at the airport.The CJP condemned the detentions in a statement, alleging that the action was pre-planned to prevent its leaders from reaching the protest site. It demanded their immediate release and described the detentions as a violation of freedom of movement.Delhi protest: Dhruv Rathee among those detainedYouTuber Dhruv Rathee has been detained by Delhi Police from his residence in Sector 56, Gurugram, sources told news agency PTI.The Cockroach Janta Party also claimed on X that Rathee had been detained, alleging that the government was afraid of young people who questioned its actions.CJP's legal head Ratna Singh was also reportedly detained from her Delhi residence, according to media reports.Meanwhile, police detained more than 200 protesters on Saturday morning ahead of the planned demonstration. Earlier, a few protesters who had started gathering at Jantar Mantar were also detained.The detentions came amid heightened security arrangements across Delhi, with police checking vehicles at border points and deploying personnel at key locations to prevent unauthorised gatherings.Nitin Nabin accuses INDIA bloc, CJP of trying to destabilise IndiaBJP president Nitin Nabin accused the INDIA bloc, led by Rahul Gandhi, and the CJP of attempting to create instability in the country.In his remarks, Nabin described the two groups as anarchic and alleged that they were competing to create unrest instead of accepting the public's electoral verdict. He further alleged that their political activities were being carried out at the behest of foreign forces, but did not provide evidence for the claim in the quoted remarks.— ANI (@ANI) Nabin also said India was progressing despite global crises and accused the Opposition of being unable to accept the country's growth and movement towards self-reliance.He asserted that Indian democracy was strong and that citizens would unite to thwart attempts to destabilise the country.Why is CJP protesting at Jantar Mantar?The CJP has called for a demonstration demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and opposing the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.The protest comes amid an escalating political confrontation between the Opposition and the Election Commission of India over allegations of 'vote chori' and concerns surrounding the revision of electoral rolls.Delhi Police denied permission for the demonstration at Jantar Mantar, citing a previous breakdown of law and order in the area.CJP activist Abhijeet Dipke criticised the government's response to the planned protest, alleging that authorities were attempting to discourage people from participating.Speaking to reporters in Mumbai before leaving for Delhi, Dipke accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of being afraid of young people who question the government. He also alleged that police personnel were visiting residential areas to discourage residents from joining the demonstration.Dipke maintained that peaceful protest was a fundamental right under Article 19 of the Constitution.Delhi Metro closes gates at 45 stationsThe Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) announced restrictions at 45 Metro stations in view of the planned demonstration and the associated security arrangements.Entry and exit gates at the affected stations were closed from 9 pm on Friday, October 9, with the restrictions scheduled to continue through Saturday evening.The measures were intended to manage crowds and maintain security around sensitive locations in the national capital. The restrictions have also affected access to stations in areas surrounding the planned protest.Commuters have been advised to check official Delhi Metro updates before travelling, as services and access arrangements may change depending on the security situation.Delhi Airport issues travel advisoryDelhi Airport has advised passengers travelling to and from the airport to plan their journeys in advance and allow additional time for their commute.The advisory was issued amid heightened security arrangements and anticipated traffic restrictions linked to the protest.“In view of the enhanced security arrangements and anticipated traffic restrictions in Delhi, passengers travelling to and from Delhi Airport are advised to plan their journeys in advance and allow additional time for their commute,” the airport said in a statement.It also advised passengers to consider alternative transport options, including cabs and city buses, where appropriate.Delhi Traffic Police separately advised commuters to keep extra travel time if heading towards railway stations, inter-state bus terminals (ISBTs) or the airport through New Delhi and Central Delhi.People were also advised to avoid non-essential travel. The police said traffic management arrangements could be adjusted based on real-time assessments of the situation.Internet services suspended near Janpath and Kartavya PathAuthorities have imposed additional restrictions in parts of central Delhi, including a temporary suspension of internet services around the Janpath-Kartavya Path crossing.Internet services were suspended within a radius of 4 km from the crossing for 24 hours, starting at 10 pm on Friday, October 9.The area is considered sensitive because of its proximity to key government buildings and other important locations.Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) has also been imposed in Delhi as authorities step up security ahead of the demonstration.Separately, Gautam Buddh Nagar Police imposed prohibitory orders across the district from Saturday morning until October 20. The restrictions prohibit gatherings of five or more people without prior permission, processions, provocative speeches and the spread of misleading information.Security tightened at Delhi borders and key locationsDelhi Police remained on high alert on Saturday, with security strengthened across the national capital and vehicle checks intensified at inter-state and inter-district borders.Police personnel were deployed at several entry points, including the Aya Nagar, Ghazipur and Badarpur borders. Barricades were installed at multiple locations, while personnel checked vehicles entering Delhi.Deputy Commissioner of Police Anant Mittal visited the Aya Nagar border to review security arrangements.Speaking to news agency IANS, Mittal said special arrangements had been made at inter-state and inter-district borders to prevent unauthorised elements from entering New Delhi and to maintain law and order.Police personnel were also equipped with body cameras to record incidents and help monitor any physical altercations during the demonstration.Drone surveillance was underway at key locations, including New Delhi Railway Station, where Delhi Police and Rapid Action Force personnel were deployed. Security marches were also conducted.Security was strengthened outside the residences of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi. Additional security personnel were deployed at sensitive locations, while roads leading towards Janpath and Mandi House witnessed barricading and checks.Train cancellations inconvenience passengersSeveral trains were cancelled amid the heightened security arrangements, causing inconvenience to passengers travelling to and from Delhi on Saturday.Passengers at railway stations reported having to change their travel plans at short notice.One passenger told IANS that trains running via Jaunpur, including the Tapti Ganga and Kashi Vishwanath Express, had been cancelled. The passenger said they might have to travel to Lucknow and change trains or take a bus to reach their destination.Another passenger travelling from Gujarat said they had faced difficulties reaching Ghaziabad after arriving at Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station, as the expected connecting trains were unavailable.However, some passengers reported that their journeys had continued without difficulty, with trains arriving at Hazrat Nizamuddin on time.Police and Rapid Action Force personnel remained deployed at railway stations, while drone surveillance and security patrols continued.Delhi protest: What should commuters keep in mind?With security measures in force across Delhi and neighbouring areas, commuters should check the latest official advisories before setting out.Metro: Check DMRC updates for restrictions on entry and exit gates at affected stations.Airport: Allow extra time for travel and consider alternative transport options.Roads: Check Delhi Traffic Police advisories before travelling through central Delhi or towards railway stations and ISBTs.Trains: Verify train status with the relevant railway authorities before leaving for the station.Internet: Be aware of the reported temporary suspension of internet services in parts of central Delhi.Authorities have said that security and traffic arrangements may be modified depending on the situation on the ground. The restrictions come as police prepare to manage the planned demonstration while maintaining law and order across the national capital.

The poll authority wrote to all state chief electoral officers to put in place the new system.
